name: smith_chart
doc:
THE SMITH CHART = THE CAYLEY TRANSFORM (Matt, 2026-10-07, RF designer's view). The reflection
coefficient Gamma = (z - 1)/(z + 1) (z = normalized impedance) is the Mobius map that carries the right
half-plane to the unit disk - the same Cayley transform that sends a SELF-ADJOINT operator to a UNITARY
one, the real line to the unit circle. The lossless (pure-reactance) impedances land exactly on |Gamma| =
1. Line <-> circle: the engineer's picture of self-adjoint <-> unitary, and of 'zeros on Re=1/2' <->
'eigenvalues on |z|=1'. Seal the three canonical loads. New stick.

sticks.question: The Smith chart - the Cayley transform
sticks.statement: Gamma = (z - 1)/(z + 1) maps the passive-impedance half-plane (Re z >= 0) into the unit disk and the lossless imaginary axis onto the unit circle |Gamma| = 1. It is the Cayley transform; the operator form (A - iI)(A + iI)^-1 sends a self-adjoint A to a unitary U, the real spectrum to the unit circle.
references: P. Smith's impedance chart (1939) - Gamma = (Z - Z0)/(Z + Z0)
the Cayley transform between self-adjoint and unitary operators
the conformal map of the half-plane onto the disk
sticks.by: Narrow Highway - the Smith chart / Cayley transform, 2026-10-07

marks.claim: [matched load -> center] z = 1 gives Gamma = (1-1)/(1+1) = 0 (sealed): a perfectly matched load sits at the center of the chart, |Gamma| = 0, no reflection. The fixed point of the transform.
[short -> the circle] z = 0 (a short) gives Gamma = (0-1)/(0+1) = -1 (sealed): on the unit circle, total reflection. Open and short sit at opposite points of |Gamma| = 1.

[lossless -> the unit circle, the key] z = i (pure reactance) gives |Gamma|^2 = ((-1)^2 + 1^2)/(1^2 + 1^2) = 2/2 = 1 (sealed), so |Gamma| = 1. EVERY lossless impedance - the whole imaginary axis - maps onto the unit circle. This is self-adjoint (spectrum on the line) <-> unitary (spectrum on the circle) in the engineer's hand: the same line<->circle symmetry that pins |alpha| = sqrt(q) over a finite field (stick_finite_field_riemann) and that Hilbert-Polya would use (stick_hilbert_polya).

[why this belongs in the Riemann arc] The Smith chart is a conformal MAP; the critical line Re(s) = 1/2 and the unit circle are two faces of one symmetry under Cayley. The engine is not an RF simulator and does not run electromagnetics; it seals the transform's arithmetic and keeps the likeness as discernment. map, never launder.
